articles.title: Pitru Paksha 2026: 3 Mistakes To Avoid Doing After Tarpan And Shraddha
articles.description:
Pitru Paksha is regarded as an important period for remembering ancestors and performing Pitru Karma with devotion. In 2026, Pitru Paksha begins on September 27 and concludes with Sarva Pitru Amavasya on October 10. During this period, families perform rituals such as Shraddha, Tarpan, Pinda Daan, Brahmin Bhojan and Daan according to their traditions.

The word Shraddha is associated with performing ancestral rituals with faith and devotion. Traditional practices place importance not only on completing the ritual but also on maintaining restraint and a sattvic way of life afterwards. So, what should devotees avoid after completing Shraddha or Tarpan?

ALSO READ: Ganeshotsav 2026: Pune’s Dagdusheth Ganpati Gets A Giant 251-Kg Modak Cake

1. Avoid Non-Sattvic Food And Indulgence

After performing Pitru Karma, devotees traditionally maintain physical and mental restraint. The focus is not limited to food but also extends to one's conduct throughout the day.

As part of these traditional practices, devotees are advised to avoid food prepared with onion and garlic. Excessive indulgence is also avoided, while a simple and sattvic lifestyle is followed.

2. Stay Away From Arguments And Harsh Words

The period after Shraddha is traditionally associated with calmness and self-control. Therefore, devotees are advised to avoid arguments, abusive language and deliberately hurting another person's feelings after returning home from the ritual.

According to traditional belief, maintaining a peaceful atmosphere is an important part of observing Pitru Karma with sincerity.

3. Avoid Cutting Hair And Nails In A Hurry

In several families, cutting hair, shaving or trimming nails is avoided on the day of Shraddha. Such activities are traditionally associated with grooming and personal adornment, while Pitru Paksha is observed as a period of restraint and solemnity.

Therefore, some families choose to postpone haircuts, shaving and nail cutting as part of their customary observances.

Why Are Tarpan And Pinda Daan Performed?

Tarpan involves offering water, along with items such as sesame seeds and Kusha, while remembering one's ancestors. Pinda Daan and Brahmin Bhojan are also regarded as important parts of Shraddha rituals.

Even after the main ritual is completed, traditional observances place emphasis on maintaining restraint and sattvic conduct for the rest of the day.

ALSO READ: Mahalaya 2026 Rituals: How To Observe Tarpan, Shradh And Pitru Puja

What Can Be Donated To A Brahmin After Pitru Tarpan?

According to the practices mentioned in the source material, devotees may offer:

  • Food Grains: Rice, wheat, pulses and flour
  • Black Sesame Seeds: Sesame holds a traditional significance in Pitru Karma
  • Clothes: Dhoti, angavastra or other new garments
  • Dakshina: A monetary offering as part of the ritual

Pitru Paksha is traditionally observed as a period of remembrance, devotion and gratitude towards ancestors. Following customary practices after Shraddha and Tarpan is considered part of maintaining the solemn spirit of the ritual.

articles.title: 10 interesting baby names that sound modern but are actually thousands of years old

articles.title: Good Boys Motion Poster Unveiled: Vennela Kishore Leads A Crazy Gang Of Entertainers
articles.description: The makers of Good Boys have officially unveiled the film's entertaining motion poster and first-look poster on the special occasion of Vennela Kishore's birthday. Written and directed by Raghav, the film is produced by Surya Gunnam, Vivek Inampudi, and Navya Sasank Kanakamedala. Right from the first look, Good Boys promises a laugh riot packed with madness, comedy, and unexpected adventures, with Vennela Kishore leading a wildly entertaining gang. The recently released "Cousins Are Coming" promotional video featuring the film's lead cast turned into a viral sensation on social media, winning audiences over with its hilarious moments and quirky characters. Now, the motion poster takes the excitement a step further by introducing the entire gang in a stylish and chaotic setup. The tagline instantly grabs attention: "They're not heroes, not even close. But they're the only ones stupid enough to take on the bad guys." That one line perfectly captures the film's fun-filled and unconventional world. Known as one of Telugu cinema's biggest entertainers, Vennela Kishore once again steals the spotlight with his trademark comic energy and effortless screen presence. The motion poster showcases him at the center of complete madness, hinting at a character that's equal parts hilarious, lovable, and unpredictable. With a talented ensemble around him, Good Boys looks set to deliver a wholesome entertainer where comedy meets chaos in the most unexpected way. The film features an exciting cast including Vennela Kishore, Shruti Sodhi, Ravi Raja, Viva Harsha, Wamce Goud, Gundu Sudarshan, Joshi Josh Creations, Hyper Aadi, Raghu Babu, Kiran Macha, Dhee Pandu, Ramana Bhargav, and Ashwini Ayaluru. The energetic motion poster has already created strong curiosity among movie lovers, with audiences praising its quirky vibe, colorful presentation, and entertaining concept. With Raghav handling the writing and direction, Good Boys promises a refreshing commercial entertainer loaded with laughter, friendship, and complete madness. The film's technical team includes Goutham Govindarajan as the cinematographer, SriCharan Pakala as the music composer, and veteran editor Marthand K. Venkatesh. Backed by Surya Gunnam, Vivek Inampudi, and Navya Sasank Kanakamedala, with Arjun Raja Dasaraju as co-producer, Good Boys is shaping up to be a fun-filled entertainer that celebrates the entertaining phenomenon called Vennela Kishore in full form. Cast: Vennela kishore, Shruti Sodhi, Ravi Raja, Viva Harsha, Wamce Goud, Gundu Sudarshan, Joshi josh creations, Hyper aadi, Raghu Babu Actor kiranmacha, Dhee pandu , Ramana Bhargav ,Ashwini Ayaluru Technical Crew: Written & Directed by : Raghav Produced by : Surya Gunnam, Vivek Inampudi, Navya Sasank Kanakamedala Co Produced by : Arjun Raja Dasaraju DOP : Goutham Govindarajan Music : Sri Charan Pakala Editor : Marthand K Venkatesh PRO : Vamsi Kaka Marketing : Housefull
